frequency_question: How often do state supreme courts successfully finalize and issue a binding ruling on a contested electoral map within 18 days of the final administrative printing deadline across comparable state jurisdictions?
membership_rule: Includes all state supreme court proceedings where a legislative or congressional map was challenged via original action, a stay or injunction was sought, and the court had 18 calendar days or fewer remaining before the mandatory state election authority ballot certification/printing deadline. Excludes federal court proceedings and cases with >18 days remaining.

skeleton: Total expedited emergency election docket cases matching sub-three-week turnaround window partitioned by whether a substantive re-drawing order or outright approval was finalized before the drop-dead ballot lock.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 7 total identified instances where an appellate court successfully navigated an 18-day or shorter operational runway without triggering a statutory ballot deadline breach.
validity_reason: State court administrative procedures and statutory ballot deadlines remain stable year-over-year, shifting only with major legislative overhauls of election codes.
